sources.content: Firms reported that their development and deployment of AI is shaped by a combination of domestic and international frameworks. sources.title: EU AI Act Readiness: A Practitioner's Guide for Corporate Leaders
sources.content:
The Act regulates AI by risk: the higher the potential harm to health, safety or fundamental rights, the heavier the obligations. It entered into force on August 1, 2024, and its obligations phase in through 2028. The Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), in force since July 27, 2026, mainly moved the high-risk deadlines back and simplified some procedures; the Act’s core requirements are unchanged.

### The EU AI Act categorizes AI systems into four risk tiers: [...] The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is the world’s first horizontal AI law, and it already applies in part. Prohibition of certain AI practices and AI literacy requirements have been enforceable since February 2025, and obligations for providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models have applied since August 2025. The Article 50 transparency requirements became legally enforceable on August 2, 2026. The heaviest obligations for high-risk AI systems will apply from December 2, 2027, for the [...] 2, 2027, for the use cases listed in Annex III and from August 2, 2028, for AI embedded in products regulated under Annex I. The July 2026 Digital Omnibus on AI deferred several key obligations for high-risk systems beyond their original August 2026 and August 2027 deadlines. However, that deferral only provides additional runway to in-scope organizations. The underlying obligations have not changed, and the time the regulator has provided should be used productively towards EU AI Act readiness

sources.title: UK ICO Secures AI Data Pledges From 10 Firms
sources.content:
The UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office said on October 8, 2026 that ten of the world’s largest AI foundation-model developers have made, or committed to make, data protection changes following its scrutiny. The list includes Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Stability AI, according to the ICO’s own announcement. The regulator says the engagement ran for roughly two years and produced clearer transparency information, stronger mechanisms for [...] How does this compare to EU or US AI regulation?  
The UK is applying its existing UK GDPR framework through the ICO rather than a dedicated AI statute. The EU has a separate AI Act alongside GDPR, while the US relies on agency-specific actions, such as FTC investigations, without a single comprehensive federal AI law. [...] ## Frequently Asked Questions

What did the UK ICO announce on October 8, 2026?  
The ICO said ten major AI foundation-model developers, Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Stability AI, have made, or committed to make, data protection changes following its supervisory engagement.

How long did the ICO’s scrutiny last?  
The regulator described the process as roughly two years of engagement with the companies involved.
